market_holds: Spot $2.95 (sealed baseline 2026-11-20 18:09 UTC; Yahoo bar shows $2.98 near the close), at its 52-week low, -6.65% over 5 days, -11.1% over 20 days, and about -24% from $3.91 on 2026-09-30 (Yahoo daily bars), on thin volume (about 56k units a day, roughly $165k). No usable option chain (empty Dec chain), no earnings-move history in the baseline, no consensus I could find, no short-interest data (NYSE-listed, Nasdaq does not serve it). Own arithmetic from the Q2 release (net income $16.0m, $0.39 per common unit) puts the units on a low single-digit earnings multiple, i.e. the price carries a large tail risk on the two Yamal Trade charters (34.5% of H1 2026 revenue), which a 2026-11-03 sanctions update said need non-UK insurers and service providers from 2027-01-01. Fully contracted fleet: 100% coverage for 2026 and 2027, 65% for 2028, $0.73bn backlog (Q2 release, 2026-09-08). Distribution $0.05 already declared 2026-11-03, the 2M-unit Series A preferred redemption ($50m) was announced 2026-10-09 and done 2026-11-12, so the quarter's capital return news is out. Past print open-gaps (prior close to first trade, Yahoo bars): Q3'25 2025-11-20 +1.4%, Q4'25 2026-03-13 +3.1%, Q1'26 2026-05-29 0.0%, Q2'26 2026-09-08 +3.8%; close-to-close on those days +6.5%, -3.6%, -2.1%, +5.5%. The unit trades on sanctions/charter survival, not on the headline EPS.
view: A fully contracted six-ship partnership whose quarter is close to known: Clean Energy on its improved Rio Grande charter from 30 April, Arctic Aurora at a lower rate, lower interest costs, Yamal hire still being received as of the 3 November update. The numbers will very likely be steady and the market does not trade on them. What moves the units is the sanctions paragraph and capital allocation. The 7-week slide from $3.91 to $2.98 lines up with sanctions risk, not with fundamentals: the US Graham Act signed in September with a 30-day review that implicates Yamal LNG's controlling shareholder (gCaptain 2026-09-21), then a broad waiver on 2026-10-16 that did not stop the slide, then the company's own 3 November warning that UK-based insurers must be replaced from 1 January 2027, with the risk of off-hire, disputes or a covenant problem. Tax-loss selling in a name at its yearly low probably adds to it. Two things in tonight's release could give a relief open: a sanctions update saying non-UK cover or providers are arranged, and renewal of the $10m buyback that expires 24 November (last year the Q3 release said it would renew, and it did on 2025-12-10). The other way, the update could repeat the 3 November warning or add charterer friction, and the units could gap lower on a thin Monday open. Past prints opened flat-to-up four times in four, which leans slightly positive, but those were all bmo prints into a less stressed tape. I lean slightly up and am not confident.
unpriced: Possibly an overshoot: the price seems to carry a full sanctions tail while hire is still being paid and the EU's 21st package keeps a legacy-contract exemption to July 2027. But I cannot show that this release will close the gap inside the window, because the decisive item (whether replacement non-UK insurance is in place for 2027) is undisclosed and could go either way. So nothing I can name as clearly unpriced.

recommendation.reason: The quarter's numbers are close to locked in by the charters, and the units trade on the sanctions disclosure, which I cannot read ahead of time. The slide into the print and the history of flat-to-up opens favour a small relief move, but the 3 November warning about replacing UK insurers from January 2027 could just as easily be repeated or made worse. That is below the 65 bar, with no mechanism I can date.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A sanctions update saying non-UK insurers or service providers are secured for Yenisei River and Lena River, plus a renewed buyback, would make me a clear long. Language that Yamal Trade disputes the charters or that cover cannot be found would make me short.

self_critique: The slide may be informed selling ahead of a worse sanctions disclosure, e.g. Yamal Trade pushing back or no non-UK insurer for 2027. A thin Friday-amc print scored at Monday's open could gap on a few hundred units, either way. The record of positive opens is four bmo prints, a tiny sample in a calmer tape. Tax-loss selling into December could hold down even a good print. This is why p_up stays at 57 and there is no recommendation.
